capture.route: In open snow, native touch drag begins at simulation tick 4, reverses direction at tick 67 and releases at tick 126. Replayed at default and 2× camera zoom. Each panel shows the complete frame above a crop of its own runner.

native_120hz_support.controls: Normal field scene. ScreenTouch + Drag. 120Hz physics, traveling against fixed world. Rendering captured separately through gameplay camera.
native_120hz_support.notes: Contact means the lower material surface of either boot. Ground is actual mesh top at Y=0, collision box top Y=0, shader has no height displacement. >1 cm is a measurement convention, not a reference-derived threshold. Each foot separately tracked. A and B recordings do not expose a ground calibration in centimetres.

native_120hz_fixed_patch.method: Actual normal-input physics at 120Hz. For each complete loading interval with minimum boot height under 6 mm, keep one original material vertex that stays in contact longest. Keep that vertex fixed until it leaves the 6 mm band. Separately report tangential velocity of the active lowest material when support rolls from heel to toe. Snow top is y=0. Values include no screen-based threshold.

footstep_alignment.method: Actual scene field event times aligned to 120 Hz physics. Compare with downward crossing of original boot material past 6 mm. A sound may occur slightly after first contact as weight loads. Boundary contacts excluded.
